title: Dispatch order: Boss receipt
summary: Topological queues. Multiply the first number in the result list by 1, the second by 2, the third by 3, and so on.
descriptionMd:
Your task
Build a result list using Step 1. Then use that list to find the answer in Step 2.

Inputs
links is a square table of 0s and 1s. Points are numbered from 0. A 1 at links[a][b] means a one-way path goes from point a to point b. A 0 means no path. k is included in the function call, but this task does not use it. You can ignore it.

Step 1: Build the result list
Each point in this graph is a task. A path from task a to task b means a must happen before b. Put all tasks with no paths coming into them in a queue, in number order. A queue serves the task at its front first. Remove that task, record its number, and remove its outgoing paths. Check its next tasks in number order. Add a task to the back of the queue as soon as it has no paths left coming in. If you cannot record every task, the rules contain a loop: use an empty result list instead.

Step 2: Return the answer
Multiply the first number in the result list by 1, the second by 2, the third by 3, and so on. Add these products and return the total. An empty list gives 0.

Write your function
Complete dispatchOrderBossReceipt(links, k). Return the answer from Step 2. Do not print it or read keyboard input. In examples, positions (indexes) start at 0 unless a rule says otherwise.

constraints: k is a whole number from 1 to 8. Answers fit in a signed 32-bit integer: -2,147,483,648 through 2,147,483,647.
Input numbers have no decimal part. They range from -1,000,000 to 1,000,000. Follow any extra input rules in Step 1.
The graph has at most 16 points. Its table has the same number of rows and columns. Link entries are 0 or 1; cost entries are 0 through 13.
Efficiency goal: time O(V^2); extra memory, including the result list, O(n). n is the input length; V is the number of graph points. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.
